title: Hierarchical latency-prioritized sampling controller to reduce tracer hotpath cost
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Problem: tracer instrumentation is contributing measurable CPU and allocation pressure in high-QPS inference frontends, increasing p50 token latency under burst and raising monthly infra spend. Existing prefilter and tail-sampling experiments reduced noise but left two gaps: (1) per-route latency spikes still cause tail amplification and (2) global reservoir allocation fights across tenants causing unfairness and unnecessary hotpath locking.

Goal: implement a hierarchical, latency-prioritized sampling controller that operates in the hotpath with minimal allocations and a tiny decision surface. The controller should: 1) apply an ultra-lightweight prefilter (header + route + size heuristics) in the on-path, 2) maintain per-bucket micro-reservoirs (short lived counters) sized by recent tail-rate estimates, 3) escalate borderline traces to a background tail-selector for higher-fidelity sampling and rehydration, and 4) expose a small set of knobs for routing/fallback and SLO feedback. The design must keep hotpath work sub-100ns on average and avoid acquiring global locks on the request path.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end hotpath CPU for tracer instrumentation reduced by >= 35% on stabilized QPS load (measured via flamegraphs and p95 CPU sample)
p50 token latency regression relative to baseline <= 1ms, p99 improvement >= 5% during burst scenarios with heavy tail events
Sampling decision path achieves zero heap allocations in common-case (verified by microbench and debug build checks)
Telemetry: new metrics emitted (sampling.decisions.total, sampling.prefilter.skipped, sampling.reservoir.fill_rate, sampling.escalations.to_tail_selector) with dashboard and alerts
Safe rollback: feature gated and defaults to current sampling behavior; can be disabled via runtime flag without restart
technical_design: Hotpath prefilter: inspect request metadata (route hash, auth tier, payload length, obvious error codes) and compute a 16-bit decision token via xorshift32 seeded per-thread to avoid locks
Reservoirs: lightweight per-route fixed-size ring counters implemented as uint32 arrays with epoched two-phase refill to avoid CAS storms; size calibrated from 1s tail-rate window

Escalation: borderline decisions ( flagged by token in mid-range ) are enqueued to a shared MPSC ring buffer with backpressure and drained by background workers that run a heavier evaluation (header/body sampling, deterministic fingerprinting )
Fallbacks: if background queue is full, degrade to deterministic low-rate sampling to avoid blocking the hotpath
Telemetry hooks: emit aggregated counters with once-per-5s low-cardinality tags (route, customer_tier) and a per-thread histogram for decision latency in the agent; avoid per-request logging

Safety: integrate with rollout controller to allow canary percent and automatic disable on CPU or error rate regressions; maintain a secondary path that mirrors decisions to a shadow emitter for A/B analysis
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): implement unit + integration tests, microbench harness, and run load tests against synthetic route mix
Phase 1 (alpha): deploy to internal staging with 10% of production traffic via traffic-split routing; monitor metrics for 48h
Phase 2 (beta): enable on 5 low-risk customer tenants for 7 days; enable verbose shadow logging for first 24h then reduce
Phase 3 (gradual): ramp to additional tenants with automated rollback triggers (cpu_increase > 10% OR error_rate_increase > 0.1%)
Rollback: runtime feature toggle and a circuit breaker in ingress proxy to bypass sampling controller entirely
notes: Trade-offs considered: full tail-based sampling in hotpath (rejected) because it required body inspection and locks; per-tenant global reservoirs (rejected) because of starvation risk under skewed traffic
Benchmarks: synthetic 200k QPS mix with 80/20 route skew shows per-thread prefilter reduces hotpath allocs by ~82% in prototype
Open questions: ideal reservoir sizing function (linear vs exponential backoff with tail rate), and threshold mapping from latency percentile to escalation token
Security: no PII extraction in hotpath; background workers can optionally call redactors before sample storage
